problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision exactly as posed: three routes (close to Central, cross-dock, retain) plus the deferral path the pack hints at, with status quo as reference. The board's own tests (net saving after routing and handling, the all-order 92% SLA, 2028 Central capacity, lease and $0.9M one-time authority) become explicit pass/fail criteria on slide 3, with reversibility added and justified. It specifies the contracted all-ZIP KPI and all-in cost rather than the CFO's transport KPI, and sets a burden of proof on the hard-to-reverse option. Nothing material to fix.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the three summary points map to slides 6-8, 9-12 and 13-16, and nearly every title is a claim its slide supports with arithmetic. Two flaws keep it from a 5. First, the headline statements 'closing East saves at most $0.10M a year' and 'keeping East is the cheapest way to meet the SLA: HOLDS' are stated categorically, yet slide 14 shows that under the alternative reading of the $0.85M minimum the cross-dock would be $0.34-0.40M a year cheaper than K. The document discloses this and labels Reading A as base case, but the top-line wording is firmer than the body. Second, there is some redundancy: slides 4, 5, 13 and 16 restate findings proven elsewhere.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived every figure I relied on and found no errors. All-in costs are right (SQ 8.74, K 8.44, C 8.64, X 8.89 in 2027; 8.99, 8.69, 8.99, 9.20 in 2028), as are the two-year totals. Net closure saving is $0.10M (1.30 - 1.00 - 0.20). Break-evens are right (220k and 160k for C; 150k and 50k for X). Weighted network SLA is 90.3% for C, 93.9% for X and 95.1% for K, with a correct 88.3% Eastern threshold. Central 2028 load is 389.6k (108%), and the Reading B arithmetic checks. All four required calculations are done transparently, and all critical evidence is used, including the 98% vs 96% rural exclusion and the confounded retention claim, which is explicitly not used as causal. Evidence against the recommendation is surfaced (Reading B, 'corrections cut both ways'). Invented inputs (the $0.25M test cap, the half-forecast low-growth case, the 2-pt rural gap) are clearly labelled as assumptions. The only overstatement is the 'at most $0.10M' headline, which the same summary qualifies; I do not judge it material.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation (Option K now, a capped all-ZIP cross-dock test through holiday and spring promotion, lease decision at a Q3 2028 gate) follows directly from the analysis and matches a defensible answer. Alternatives are compared on the stated criteria in a scorecard, with 'unproven' explicitly not counted as a pass. Trade-offs are explicit: cost vs service, exit fee and two-year minimum vs waiting for the lease end, and the cross-dock relieving Central but adding unproven third-party dependence. It says what would change the answer through four quantified gate criteria and volume break-evens, and gives a guardrail for K (East all-ZIP at or above 95%). It also handles the K saving not materialising and names the unstated East capacity. It avoids all four traps. The test design depends on the provider agreeing to no two-year minimum, which is flagged as needing agreement.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on the title slide and in the executive summary, the language is plain, and the arithmetic is shown inline. But 18 slides and about 4,650 words is more than this decision needs. Slides 4 (hypothesis table), 5 (claims table), 13 (scorecard) and 16 (risks) repeat results established on the analytic slides, and slide 8's break-even largely overlaps slide 6 and slide 14. Strong, but not every slide earns its place.

unsupported_claims.quote: Closing East saves at most $0.10M a year, not the $1.3M claimed
unsupported_claims.why: True only for close-to-Central or under the base reading of the cross-dock quote. The document's own Reading B sensitivity shows the cross-dock closure would be $0.34-0.40M a year cheaper than K, so 'at most' is overstated for an ambiguity the pack does not resolve.

unsupported_claims.quote: Option K beats the status quo by $0.30M a year at low risk
unsupported_claims.why: The $0.30M is an unverified audit estimate, and the pack gives no risk assessment of the shift renegotiation. The document itself later flags that the saving may not materialise and that shift changes could hurt service.

unsupported_claims.quote: Peak weeks carry the most service risk
unsupported_claims.why: Plausible, but the pack only says the pilot excluded holiday weeks and that the operator has not guaranteed the spring promotion. It gives no data on peak-week service performance.

recommendation.summary: Keep East open in 2027 and do not serve the East from Central. Approve Option K ($0.30M a year saving for $0.15M one-time). Authorise a capped (up to $0.25M) all-ZIP cross-dock test through holiday 2027 and the spring 2028 promotion with no two-year minimum. Take the 2029 lease decision at a Q3 2028 board gate with four quantified criteria.
recommendation.rationale: Meets all four defensibility criteria. It models all-in cost (net closure saving $0.10M, full option cost tables). It weights the SLA across all 500k shipments on the all-ZIP definition (90.3% for closure). It recognises the 2028 Central breach (389.6k vs 360k). It quantifies realistic alternatives (K, cross-dock under two contract readings) with an explicit decision gate.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The document treats the CEO's 'keep East' view as a working hypothesis, breaks it into five testable conditions, and concludes it holds with three refinements: optimise rather than just retain; capacity rules out only close-to-Central, not the cross-dock; keep through 2029 rather than permanently, with a gated cross-dock test. This matches the expected keep-with-conditions handling. It tests the CEO's unproven 'cheapest way to meet the SLA' claim on cost. It corrects the pro-retention claims (98% vs 96%, the confounded 8-pt renewal premium) as well as the pro-closure ones. It refuses to use the retention correlation as causal evidence.

output.overall_comment: Very strong document; weighted score 4.65. Every number I rechecked against the pack is correct, and all four required calculations are done transparently. It goes beyond the key with break-even volumes, the 88.3% Eastern threshold that keeps the network at 92%, a rural-exclusion sensitivity on the pilot, and the ambiguity over whether the $0.85M cross-dock minimum is a fixed fee or a credited spend floor. It avoids all four traps, handles the CEO's hypothesis as keep-with-conditions, and gives an executable plan with quantified gate criteria. Two weaknesses: the headline 'at most $0.10M' and 'cheapest way to meet the SLA: HOLDS' are stated more categorically than the document's own Reading B sensitivity allows, and at 18 slides with several recap tables it is longer than the decision needs. The feasibility and $0.25M cost of a cross-dock test without a two-year minimum is an assumption, though it is flagged as such.
